cards.title: Earn backlinks on educational posts, then pass the authority to money pages with internal links
cards.summary: Top-of-funnel guides are easier to link to than sales pages; transfer that link equity to product and category pages through contextual internal links.
cards.use_when: Link building and internal linking plan for an ecommerce catalog, when deciding which URLs to pitch for links.

cards.title: Two-Channel Visibility: Traditional SEO as the Foundation for AI Search
cards.summary: AI assistants retrieve answers using traditional search indexes, so ranking in Google/Bing remains the prerequisite for appearing in AI answers.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in SEO at all versus chasing AI-search visibility for your store's product and category pages.

cards.title: Run the 30-Second Intent Test Before Targeting Any Keyword
cards.summary: Search your target keyword and read the top 10 results; the format that ranks is Google's definition of the intent you must match.
cards.use_when: Validating keyword targets for a product page, category page, comparison page or blog post before committing content budget.

cards.title: The Keyword Sweet Spot Framework: Demand, Fit, Intent, Difficulty
cards.summary: Score every keyword candidate on four attributes — real search demand, funnel fit, satisfiable intent, and realistic rankability — before choosing targets.
cards.use_when: Filtering a raw keyword list down to the targets worth building store pages or content around.

cards.title: Money Pages First: Build Conversion Pages Before Informational Content
cards.summary: Prioritize the bottom-funnel product, service, pricing and feature pages that convert before writing any top-funnel blog content, so traffic always has a destination.
cards.use_when: Deciding what to build first when starting or reviving an ecommerce site's SEO program.

cards.title: Topical Authority Clusters: Why Google Evaluates Your Whole Site
cards.summary: Google assesses whether your site covers a full topic journey, so comprehensive cluster coverage makes every keyword in that cluster easier to rank.
cards.use_when: Planning which content to publish next to lift rankings for competitive product or category keywords.

cards.title: Keyword Ideation: Mine Google's Own Data Before Reaching for Tools
cards.summary: Use Search Console, autocomplete, People Also Ask, People Also Search For and community language to generate keyword ideas from real searcher phrasing.
cards.use_when: Building the seed keyword list for a new category page, buying guide or content cluster.

cards.title: Keyword Validation and Clustering With AI
cards.summary: Validate keyword ideas on volume, difficulty, fit and intent, then group topically related keywords into clusters — work that AI has made dramatically faster.
cards.use_when: Turning a raw keyword spreadsheet into a prioritized, organized content plan for your store.

cards.title: Content Creation Blueprint: Research, Structure, Write, Optimize
cards.summary: Work through four phases — competitive research, intent-matched outline, expertise-loaded draft, data-driven optimization — instead of writing straight into a blank page.
cards.use_when: Producing a product category page, buying guide or cluster article that must outrank existing results.

cards.title: Build Human Content Moats into AI-Assisted Drafts
cards.summary: Insert original data, real examples, expert insight and strong opinions into AI-generated drafts so content can differentiate in a sea of AI slop.
cards.use_when: Publishing category, guide or landing content where competitors are also using AI to mass-produce pages.

cards.title: On-Page Checklist Applied to Both Money Pages and Content Pages
cards.summary: Run the same technical checklist — title, headers, URL, meta description, internal links, images — but execute it differently for selling pages versus teaching pages.
cards.use_when: Publishing or refreshing any product page, category page or cluster article and preparing it for indexing and clicks.

cards.title: Internal Linking as the Connective Tissue of Your Funnel
cards.summary: Contextual internal links are how Google discovers content and understands page relationships — and how cluster traffic reaches your money pages.
cards.use_when: Publishing any new cluster article, guide or category page on an ecommerce site.

cards.title: Link Building: Be the Source, Then Use Journalist Queries
cards.summary: Earn high-authority backlinks by publishing original data and resources others must cite, and by responding to journalist sourcing queries daily.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to build domain authority for a store or brand whose product pages need to rank against established competitors.

cards.title: Create Linkable Assets: Tools, Calculators and Templates as Backlink Magnets
cards.summary: Free interactive tools and reference resources attract links because they make other people's content better, and AI coding tools make building them feasible for non-technical marketers.
cards.use_when: Seeking a scalable, non-outreach link acquisition method for a product category where informational guides already exist.

cards.title: Technical SEO Triage: Audit With a Crawler Instead of a Rabbit Hole
cards.summary: Most small and mid-size sites on modern platforms are already mostly technically sound; a free crawler audit surfaces the prioritized issues worth fixing.
cards.use_when: Checking whether technical problems are blocking your store's product and category pages from ranking.

cards.title: AI Search Optimization: Structured Content, Clusters and Third-Party Citations
cards.summary: To appear in AI assistant answers, use the same foundations as SEO — comprehensive structured content, topical clusters, and citations from authoritative sites that AI models weight.
cards.use_when: Trying to get your store or brand recommended when customers ask ChatGPT, Perplexity or Gemini for product recommendations.

cards.title: Zero-Click Era: Make Content Deeper Than the AI Overview
cards.summary: AI overviews now summarize commercial and transactional queries too, so surface-level pages lose the click — depth beyond the summary is the price of entry.
cards.use_when: Planning category and buying-guide content for queries where Google now shows an AI overview.

cards.title: 30-Day SEO Action Plan for a Store
cards.summary: A four-week sequence — foundation, most important money page, first funnel, promote and monitor — that installs the system even though rankings take longer.
cards.use_when: Kicking off or restarting an ecommerce SEO program with limited time and needing a concrete order of operations.

cards.title: Track SEO Progress With Leading Indicators, Not Just Clicks
cards.summary: Early SEO signals appear in Search Console before clicks do, so monitor impressions, new keyword entries and position movement to judge whether the program is working.
cards.use_when: Reviewing whether a newly published store page or cluster is gaining traction after the first weeks.

cards.title: Use Published Claude Artifacts as High-Authority Parasite SEO Hosts
cards.summary: Publish a Claude-generated article as a public artifact on claude.ai to borrow the root domain's authority and rank fast for brand and bottom-of-funnel terms.
cards.use_when: You need a brand-owned page or landing page to appear on Google quickly — e.g., brand-name searches, local SEO terms, or bottom-of-funnel keywords — and building a real page on your own site would take days.

cards.title: Prioritize Bottom-of-Funnel SEO Pages Over Cold-Audience Content
cards.summary: The source argues bottom-of-funnel pages targeting people ready to act convert far better than skyscraper-style top-of-funnel articles aimed at cold searchers.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to allocate SEO effort — e.g., choosing which landing pages or keyword pages to build next for your store.

cards.title: Exploit Relaxed Local Communities for Parasite SEO
cards.summary: Local subreddits and similar low-moderation communities let local businesses place links and posts that rank or drive traffic, unlike tightly-moderated national communities.
cards.use_when: Running local SEO or acquisition for a store with a physical or regional presence and looking for cheap ranking channels.

cards.title: Track organic search performance with GA4, GSC and GTM
cards.summary: Set up the free Google measurement stack to monitor organic traffic, indexation and on-site conversion events like add-to-cart.
cards.use_when: You need a baseline measurement of your store's SEO performance before making merch, PDP or content decisions.

cards.title: Prioritise rivals that outrank you, not the whole category
cards.summary: In competitor analysis for SEO, only study sites ranking above you and copy their keyword and content advantages.
cards.use_when: You are deciding which competitor PDPs, category pages or content to study when planning SEO or merchandising for a store.

cards.title: Set 160-character meta descriptions with the key phrase
cards.summary: Write unique, natural-language meta descriptions under ~160 characters containing the page's target phrase.
cards.use_when: You are writing or auditing title tags and meta descriptions for product, category or landing pages.

cards.title: Choose keywords by search volume plus difficulty, not volume alone
cards.summary: Screen keywords for minimum monthly searches and achievable difficulty before committing content or pages to them.
cards.use_when: You are selecting keywords for a new category page, PDP copy or blog post to support organic acquisition.

cards.title: Fix page speed before chasing rankings
cards.summary: Measure speed on mobile and desktop, then fix the specific blocking assets flagged rather than guessing.
cards.use_when: Your store pages feel slow, you suspect speed is suppressing rankings or conversions, or you are auditing the site before scaling content.

cards.title: Make URLs readable and every page HTTPS
cards.summary: Use descriptive, readable URL slugs and serve the whole store over HTTPS as baseline on-page hygiene.
cards.use_when: You are setting up or cleaning URL structure across product, collection and landing pages.

cards.title: Use sitemaps to help crawlers discover store URLs
cards.summary: Submit a sitemap so search engines know which pages exist and can crawl them, rather than waiting passively.
cards.use_when: You have new collections or product pages that are not appearing in organic search, or your catalogue is large enough that manual discovery is impractical.

cards.title: Understand the crawl-index-rank pipeline applied to your store
cards.summary: Search results are produced in three stages — crawlers, indexing and ranked display — and SEO work maps to each.
cards.use_when: You are diagnosing why a page isn't ranking and need to know which stage is failing.

cards.title: Judge directories and listings by relevance, niche and authority
cards.summary: When pursuing directory or catalogue listings, prioritise relevant, authorised placements over cheap volume.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to pay for a directory submission, marketplace listing or sponsored catalogue placement for your products.

cards.title: Split SEO work into on-page, off-page and technical buckets
cards.summary: Allocate effort across three workstreams so store optimisation is systematic rather than ad hoc.
cards.use_when: You are planning an SEO roadmap and deciding what to fix first across product pages, links and site infrastructure.

cards.title: Build an engaging on-page experience, not just keywords
cards.summary: Readable, navigable pages with clear structure support both rankings and conversion on landing and category pages.
cards.use_when: You are structuring a category, product or landing page for both search relevance and purchase conversion.

cards.title: Keep content on-topic and cite real sources
cards.summary: Publish content only around your actual product niche, and reference credible sources to build authority.
cards.use_when: You are writing blog posts or buying-guide content intended to attract organic traffic to a product category.

cards.title: Avoid black-hat tactics that risk store penalisation
cards.summary: Know the manipulative techniques Google penalises and keep your store's SEO within guidelines.
cards.use_when: You are auditing past SEO work, buying links, or reviewing an agency's or freelancer's methods before approving them.

cards.title: Frame SEO as a long-term, measurable but unguaranteed investment
cards.summary: Set expectations that organic results take time and cannot be date-guaranteed, while still measuring outcomes.
cards.use_when: You are forecasting organic growth, setting timelines with stakeholders, or deciding how much budget to hold back for paid channels.

cards.title: Use question data to improve content and product decisions
cards.summary: Mine customer questions and reviews for the queries and concerns to address in content and merchandising.
cards.use_when: You want to decide which questions to answer on PDPs or in content, or identify product objections to fix.

cards.title: Assume algorithms and search behaviour shift, and adapt
cards.summary: Treat ongoing algorithm updates and changing customer behaviour as a standing constraint on SEO plans.
cards.use_when: You are maintaining an existing SEO programme or deciding how often to revisit keyword and content strategy.

cards.title: Audit H1-H6 heading hierarchy on a product or category page
cards.summary: Use browser search to verify one H1 per page and check that H2/H3 subheadings structure product and category copy for readability and rankings.
cards.use_when: Auditing a PDP, collection page or landing page for on-page SEO before or after a content refresh.

cards.title: Write concise, descriptive titles for product and collection pages
cards.summary: Use accurate page titles rather than a fixed 160-character rule.
cards.use_when: Writing or rewriting title tags for product, category or blog pages before an SEO or paid-search push.

cards.title: Build and submit an XML sitemap to help Google discover sellable URLs
cards.summary: Create an XML sitemap listing your pages, confirm it exposes product/category/blog URLs, and submit it so search engines can crawl and index them.
cards.use_when: Launching a new store, adding a large batch of SKUs or categories, or diagnosing why pages aren't indexed.

cards.title: Use canonical tags to prevent duplicate product and category pages from competing
cards.summary: Inspect canonical tags to confirm each product/category URL self-references, signalling uniqueness and blocking duplicate-content dilution.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing cannibalized rankings after variant URLs, filters, or syndicated product copy create near-duplicates.

cards.title: Speed up load times by compressing images and video
cards.summary: Diagnose FCP/LCP in PageSpeed Insights and Search Console, then compress media to hit the source's one-to-two-second load target and reduce bounce.
cards.use_when: Improving storefront load speed when media-heavy PDPs or category pages bounce visitors or score low on mobile.

cards.title: Optimize URLs for clarity and crawlability
cards.summary: Make URLs readable and keyword-relevant, and keep stray numbers, question marks and equals signs out of customer-facing page addresses.
cards.use_when: Setting up new product or category URL structures, or cleaning up messy legacy URLs before SEO work.

cards.title: Make the mobile experience the primary storefront design
cards.summary: Design and audit the store for phones first — responsive layout, visible options and touch-friendly interaction — since most purchasing happens on mobile.
cards.use_when: Reviewing store design or a PDP/checkout experience where mobile bounce or drop-off is high.

cards.title: Design an SEO-friendly site architecture with navigation and interlinking
cards.summary: Structure categories and internal links so visitors navigate confidently and crawlers spread authority evenly and reach every page.
cards.use_when: Planning or fixing store information architecture, category hierarchy, or internal linking before scaling a catalog.

cards.title: Use Yoast (or an equivalent SEO plugin) for WordPress store page metadata and sitemaps
cards.summary: Manage WordPress page titles, descriptions, schemas, sitemaps and 404 handling through an SEO plugin, treating it as configuration rather than magic.
cards.use_when: Maintaining on-page SEO on a WordPress or WooCommerce store without hand-editing templates.

cards.title: Implement schema markup to win rich results for products and reviews
cards.summary: Generate schema JSON-LD with a tool, validate it, and have it installed so Google can surface star ratings, prices and offers in results.
cards.use_when: PDP or category SEO work where you want review stars, price and availability displayed in search results to lift click-through.

cards.title: Set up robots.txt to guide crawlers away from cart, checkout and admin URLs
cards.summary: Use robots.txt to disallow crawler access to irrelevant or private paths and direct crawl attention to product, category and content pages.
cards.use_when: Technical SEO audit on a store where crawl budget is being spent on admin, cart or checkout URLs instead of sellable pages.

cards.title: Understand crawl, index and rank mechanics to diagnose ranking problems
cards.summary: Explain how crawlers seed from indexed URLs, follow links and store content — and use that to reason about why pages aren't ranking.
cards.use_when: Investigating why new pages or products aren't appearing in search despite good content, or comparing your crawl coverage to a competitor's.

cards.title: Choose keyword research tools by job: domain/catalog audit vs. traffic analysis
cards.summary: Use a domain-level tool to audit what your site already ranks for and where backlinks exist, and a flow tool to examine traffic and keyword movement.
cards.use_when: Starting SEO work on an existing store and deciding what keywords, pages and backlinks you already have before optimizing.

cards.title: Build link authority through third-party backlinks and guest posts
cards.summary: Earn inbound links on relevant external sites using keyword anchor text, and treat links as harder to win from high-authority domains.
cards.use_when: Off-page SEO planning when you need to build domain trust and referral traffic to product or category pages.

cards.title: Run local SEO with NAP-consistent business listings and near-me keywords
cards.summary: Claim and maintain a Google Business Profile with exact name, address and phone, then target location-modified keywords for map-pack visibility.
cards.use_when: Local or multi-location stores wanting visibility in map results and 'near me' searches.

cards.title: Use YouTube SEO to drive store discovery and traffic
cards.summary: Create audience-specific videos with keyworded titles, descriptions and thumbnails, and link back to the store to grow visibility and traffic.
cards.use_when: Adding video to the acquisition mix for product education, unboxing, or how-to content that should feed the store.

cards.title: Write engaging content that keeps shoppers on the page and clicking
cards.summary: Produce valuable, relevant content so visitors stay, engage and act — reducing bounce and increasing clicks on add-to-cart and contact actions.
cards.use_when: Improving PDP copy, category descriptions or blog content that currently gets traffic but no engagement.

cards.title: Audit technical SEO health: HTTPS, responsiveness, load time, sitemap, schema, citations
cards.summary: Run through the source's technical-SEO checklist — security, responsiveness, speed, sitemap, schema, citations and error fixes — to keep a store crawlable and rankable.
cards.use_when: Periodic technical SEO audit of a store, or as a pre-launch checklist for a new site or replatform.

cards.title: Keep technical SEO current as search algorithms change
cards.summary: Treat algorithm updates as recurring filters that remove irrelevant results, and keep updating site structure, features and content to stay compliant.
cards.use_when: Planning an SEO roadmap or deciding how much to invest in technical maintenance versus one-off optimizations.

cards.title: Robots.txt: Block Admin and Cart Paths, Keep Product Pages Crawlable
cards.summary: Configure robots.txt to keep bots out of CMS admin and internal paths while allowing product, service, blog and About pages to be indexed.
cards.use_when: Setting up or auditing crawl access on a store's robots.txt before launch, migration or after adding a new CMS/app path.

cards.title: Use Google Keyword Planner for Seed and Long-Tail Keyword Discovery
cards.summary: Mine Google Keyword Planner's search volume, competition and bid data to build an SEO keyword list, including long-tail variants.
cards.use_when: Building or expanding the keyword target list for category pages, product pages or blog content.

cards.title: Use Google Trends to Time Content and Compare Keyword Demand
cards.summary: Compare keyword interest over time, by region and against alternatives in Google Trends to prioritise and schedule keywords.
cards.use_when: Deciding which keyword to target first, whether a trend is rising or dying, or which region to prioritise for a category launch.

cards.title: Page Speed Thresholds and Mobile-First Priority
cards.summary: Treat load time as a bounce driver: the source cites abandonment past 3 seconds and recommends targeting 1–2 seconds, with mobile checked separately.
cards.use_when: Auditing store speed before a traffic push, after adding apps/scripts, or when diagnosing a mobile conversion gap.

cards.title: Set Up Analytics and Understand Its Hard Start Date
cards.summary: Install Google Analytics to see traffic by channel, and accept that historical data before installation does not exist.
cards.use_when: Standing up measurement for a new store or diagnosing which channels (organic, paid, referral, email) actually drive sessions.

cards.title: Read Search Console Impressions, Clicks and CTR Without Panicking
cards.summary: Use Search Console to read query-level visibility and clicks and to expect impressions to greatly exceed clicks.
cards.use_when: Reviewing SEO performance, finding under-clicked pages, or checking for 404s the crawler discovered.

cards.title: Fix 404s by Redirecting to the Nearest Relevant Page
cards.summary: Identify broken URLs in Search Console and redirect each to the closest topical match — not to a generic page.
cards.use_when: After a product discontinuation, URL change, category reshuffle or migration creates broken links.

cards.title: Site Settings: Name, URL, Favicon and Tagline in Your CMS
cards.summary: Configure core site identity fields — site title, tagline, URL and favicon — from the CMS settings panel.
cards.use_when: Launching a new store, rebranding, or checking brand presentation in tabs and search results.

cards.title: Google Panda: Diagnose Thin and Duplicate Content Before It Suppresses Rankings
cards.summary: Recognise Panda-style quality problems — thin, duplicated, keyword-stuffed content — and run the recovery checklist the source provides.
cards.use_when: A store's category or blog pages stop ranking and you suspect thin, duplicated or stuffed content across many URLs.

cards.title: Investigate suspected manipulative backlinks before considering disavow
cards.summary: Separate actual link-scheme problems from unsolicited spam before taking action.
cards.use_when: After a sudden ranking drop, or as a routine audit when many low-quality sites link to the store.

cards.title: Judge a Link by Location, Anchor Text and Source Authority
cards.summary: Evaluate link value using the criteria search engines are described as using: page location, domain authority, anchor text, uniqueness and page rank.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to pursue or accept a link placement, or when comparing link opportunities for a product or category page.

cards.title: Land Guest Posts via 'Write For Us' and Resource-Page Prospecting
cards.summary: Find guest-post and resource pages with search operators, then pitch relevant, well-structured content in exchange for a contextual link.
cards.use_when: Building off-page links for a product category or blog, especially for niche ecommerce verticals.

cards.title: Reverse-Engineer Competitor Backlinks Before Spending on Link Building
cards.summary: Compare your backlink count and quality to a competitor's, then target the pages already linking to them.
cards.use_when: Planning a link-building campaign for a category and deciding where to invest effort first.

cards.title: Directory Submission Done Selectively and Correctly
cards.summary: Submit the store to a small number of high-authority directories with accurate titles, descriptions and categories.
cards.use_when: Adding foundational brand citations for a new store, especially for local or niche discovery.

cards.title: Syndicate and Distribute Content Without Triggering Duplicate-Content Risk
cards.summary: Use content syndication platforms to widen distribution and earn links, while keeping the original content unique to one site.
cards.use_when: Extending the reach of an existing article or guide to earn referral traffic and brand mentions.

cards.title: Use Social Posts as Link Vehicles with Clear CTAs
cards.summary: Structure social media posts so they carry a keyword, a link and a CTA that drives qualified traffic to a store page.
cards.use_when: Promoting a category, offer or guide on social channels to earn traffic and engagement alongside SEO.

cards.title: Design UI/UX Around the Cart and Checkout Actions
cards.summary: Treat the add-to-cart, checkout and place-order interactions as SEO-relevant UX: they must be obvious, working and frictionless.
cards.use_when: Reviewing PDP and cart usability, or diagnosing drop-off between product view and order placement.

cards.title: Use Customer Feedback to Feed Content and Keyword Selection
cards.summary: Collect feedback and observe user behaviour to identify what your audience actually searches for, then build content and SEO around it.
cards.use_when: Planning content, PDP copy or FAQ pages and needing evidence of real customer questions.

cards.title: Incentive-Based Link Building: Discount Offers for Links, and Its Risks
cards.summary: Offer value (discounts or promotion) to sites in exchange for a link, but only when the placement retains editorial quality.
cards.use_when: Considering a reciprocal or incentivised link arrangement where you would otherwise not earn a placement.

cards.title: Match Inbound Link Relevance to Your Target Market Region
cards.summary: Ensure inbound links come from sites relevant to your market, including geographic relevance, to avoid wasted link equity.
cards.use_when: Auditing an existing backlink profile or pre-screening link prospects for a region-specific store.

cards.title: Understand How Search Engines Evaluate Ecommerce Sites
cards.summary: Search engines judge ecommerce value through response speed, cross-engine comparison, click/eye-tracking behaviour and brand strength.
cards.use_when: Prioritising technical and brand investments for a store, or explaining why a page with good content may still rank poorly.

cards.title: Classify queries into informational, navigational and transactional buckets
cards.summary: Use the three-query-type framework to match page formats to searcher intent and avoid ranking content in the wrong slot.
cards.use_when: Planning which pages to build (PDPs, collection pages, guides, brand pages) or auditing why an existing page attracts traffic that does not convert.

cards.title: Build product pages that satisfy transactional intent end to end
cards.summary: A complete PDP should showcase, inform, differentiate and answer objections, with schema markup to win rich results.
cards.use_when: Writing or rewriting a product page description for a store, or diagnosing a PDP that gets traffic but few add-to-carts.
